title: ALMA-IMF: XXII. Role of core subfragmentation in the IMF origin: Hierarchical mass cascade in W43-MM1
question: How does the currently observed top-heavy core mass function (CMF) in the massive protocluster W43-MM1 evolve due to core subfragmentation?

data.sensitivity: Noise: <1.1, 2.5, 8, 35, and 450 MJy sr^-1 for 2.6'', 1.45'', 0.43'', 0.12'', and 0.050'' images; line noise 50 mK (Cycle 6) and 4-5 K (Cycle 7)

what.value: 3 mm continuum image of W43-MM1 from the ALMA-IMF Large Program

evidence.loc: Data reduction of the ALMA images targeting W43-MM1
evidence.quote: We used the 3 mm continuum image of ALMA-IMF, which was reduced using CASA as described in companion paper, Paper II (cite: ginsburg2022).

what.value: Synthetic compact source catalogs and 250 um synthetic observations of Orion-like MHD and HD RAMSES simulations

evidence.quote: For test and initial comparison purposes, we used source catalogs derived from synthetic images of numerical simulations designed to represent the Orion protocluster (cite: louvet2021simu).

what.value: Hierarchical cascade and fractality measurements of the NGC 2264 protocluster

evidence.loc: Characterization of the hierarchical mass cascade
evidence.quote: along with those estimated by (cite: thomasson2022; thomasson2024) for the NGC 2264 protocluster.

what.value: 127 W43-MM1 core catalog from 1.3 mm ALMA-IMF denoised image with updated dust temperatures and masses

evidence.quote: The 127 W43-MM1 cores were extracted from the best-sensitivity denoised image of the ALMA-IMF Large Program at 1.3 mm (cite: nony2023).
Their masses and uncertainties were updated by (cite: motte2025) using carefully determined dust temperatures.

recipe.goal: Reduce and image multi-resolution 3 mm ALMA continuum datasets of W43-MM1
recipe.method: Use the Cycle 5 ALMA-IMF 3 mm mosaic reduced in CASA (robust 0), and process Cycle 6 and Cycle 7 single-pointing datasets in IMAGER with line filtering above 1 sigma, phase and amplitude self-calibration, and Clark deconvolution using natural (robust 2 at ~85 GHz) and uniform (robust -2 at ~99 GHz) weighting
key_parameters: robust = 0 (Cycle 5); robust = 2 at ~85 GHz and robust = -2 at ~99 GHz (Cycle 6 and 7)
Continuum bandwidth = 1.875 GHz per band, line filter threshold = 1 sigma (50 mK for Cycle 6, 4-5 K for Cycle 7)
assumptions: Distance to W43-MM1 = 5.5 +/- 0.4 kpc; 3 mm emission is dominated by optically thin thermal dust emission

recipe.goal: Extract compact source catalogs across five spatial resolutions and rescale synthetic catalogs
recipe.method: Extract compact sources in the five W43-MM1 3 mm images using spatial decomposition and background subtraction in getsf; rescale synthetic 250 um RAMSES catalogs from 1.75 kpc to 550 pc and divide fluxes by 1.2e3 to represent 3 mm emission
key_parameters: Maximum source size = 3 times the beam of each image
assumptions: 20 K modified blackbody with dust emissivity law kappa(nu) proportional to nu^1.5 for synthetic flux rescaling; interferometric filtering does not significantly affect compact source fluxes

recipe.goal: Construct multiscale networks of nested sources and compute cascade parameters (fractality index, mass transfer efficiency, mass partition)
recipe.method: Apply graph-theory tool FAMILY to link parent and child sources across resolutions, classify structures as hierarchical, linear, or isolated, compute median 2D fractality index F_2D, correct for 3D projection effects to obtain F_3D, and measure median flux/mass transfer efficiency and sibling mass ratio/partition
key_parameters: Minimum overlap coefficient = 75% of the child area, with sources modeled as ellipses of outer diameter 2*FWHM / sqrt(2 ln 2)
assumptions: Self-similar and homogeneous cascade at first order; protostellar fragments remain dynamically coupled to parental cloud hierarchy; constant temperature between sibling children for mass partition

recipe.goal: Fit the CMF and simulate the subfragmentation cascade to predict the seed mass function and emerging IMF
recipe.method: Fit the high-mass end of the 127 W43-MM1 core mass function above 1.6 M_sun with a power law; generate 100,000 realizations of 2400 au cores and apply the Thomasson et al. (2026) stochastic gravo-turbulent cascade model down to 200 au seeds using the measured W43-MM1 cascade parameters, plus an optional mass-growth prescription, then fit the high-mass power-law slope
key_parameters: s_core = 2400 au, s_seed = 200 au, F_3D = 1.19 +/- 0.10, epsilon_jump2 = 60% +/- 25%, MP = [2/3 ; 1/3], 100,000 datasets, 10% core discount, completeness = 1.6 M_sun (cores), 0.17 M_sun (seeds), 0.18 M_sun (grown reservoirs)
assumptions: Core masses dominate protostellar embryo masses; cascade parameters remain constant down to disk scale (~200 au, with R_disk proportional to M_star^(1/3) and 50 au for solar-type stars); mass growth rate mu = M_seed / 5 M_sun

evidence.quote: The mass partition of fragments in W43-MM1 could therefore be imbalanced, MP(Primary; Secondary) $\simeq [\frac{2}{3} \,;\, \frac{1}{3}]$

answer_key.quantity: Core formation efficiency (CFE) from 2400 au cores to 200 au seeds in W43-MM1

evidence.quote: The mass transfer efficiency, computed from one physical scale to another, is high and corresponds to a core formation efficiency (CFE) from 2400 au cores to 200 au seeds of $\sim$16%.
According to \[eq:eff\] and with $\overline{\epsilon_{\rm jump2}} = 60\%$ (see Sect. 4.3), the efficiency of the formation of seeds is $\epsilon^{\rm2400~au}_{\rm 200~au}\simeq$16%.

answer_key.quantity: Predicted CFE from 30 kau clumps to 2 kau cores in W43-MM1

evidence.loc: Fragmentation levels, CFE, and fragmentation regime
evidence.quote: According to \[eq:eff\] and $\overline{\epsilon_{\rm jump2}} \simeq 60\%$, the CFE of 2 kau cores within 30 kau clumps is predicted to be $\rm \epsilon^{clump}_{cores} \simeq 14\%$.

answer_key.quantity: Average number of 200 au seeds per 2400 au core in W43-MM1 (n_seed)

evidence.quote: a W43-MM1 core detected at a scale of $s_{\rm core}=2400$ au will fragment into $n_{\rm seed}\simeq1.9$ seeds of scale $s_{\rm seed}=200$ au.

answer_key.quantity: High-mass end power-law slope of the W43-MM1 CMF (alpha)

evidence.quote: Doing so, we measured a CMF high-mass end slope of $\alpha=-1.03^{+0.09}_{-0.16}$ (see 7a), which is consistent with the values reported in (cite: motte2018b) and (cite: nony2023), and which confirms its top-heavy nature.

answer_key.quantity: High-mass end power-law slope of the predicted W43-MM1 seed mass function (alpha)

evidence.quote: Above the completeness level of $\sim$$0.17~\mbox{$M_\odot$}$, their high-mass end is fitted with the same procedure as for the CMF by a power-law of the form $\frac{dN}{d\log M} \propto M^\alpha$ with $\alpha=-0.92^{+0.06}_{-0.09}$.

answer_key.quantity: High-mass end power-law slope of the W43-MM1 gas reservoir mass function including mass growth (alpha)

evidence.quote: The power-law fitted above the new completeness limit of $0.18~\mbox{$M_\odot$}$ becomes even flatter: $\frac{dN}{d\log M} \propto M^{-0.83}$.
